It is a seamless ground/water tile, not a standing object. No front-edge line, eave shadow, ellipse, or front face is drawn. The column scans show only repeating water color (#4a7387) with scattered green sprout pixels and a darker shadow pixel, so the 3/4 top-and-front rules do not apply.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate renders as a single small tile with a speckled, rippled water-and-soil look. It has 8 visible tones per tile, against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference, so it is at or above both. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. A ground patch has no outline to judge, and the 0% neutral dark-edge share means no black sticker line. The 8 colours form roughly 5 usable lightness steps, close to the reference ramps. Texture is mostly fine dither and speckle rather than larger clumps, so I rate it 'some' rather than 'rich'. It is not thinner or flatter than the references, so a careful artist would accept it beside them.
